Regionalize a station variable over the working grid

Source: R/regionalize.R
ef_regionalize.Rd

Fits a regionalization method to the station values of one variable at each target time and predicts it exactly at every cell of the working grid (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md sections 2, 5 and 6). The method is chosen with ef_method_gwr() (C3), ef_method_station() (C1), ef_method_ols() or ef_method_idw() (C2); all return the same earthflux_surface, so that the configurations of dev/VALIDATION_PLAN.md section 2.2 differ only in method.

Steps: (1) the station coordinates (WGS84 longitude and latitude) are projected to the CRS of the grid, which must be projected in metres; (2) the covariates are extracted at the stations from the same rasters (cell containing the station, no interpolation) or taken from station_covariates; (3) stations whose QC status is not in use_qc, excluded by the user, or with a missing value, coordinate or covariate are excluded with their reason (nothing is removed silently); (4) one fit per target time; (5) block-wise prediction with terra, writing the surface and a flag word per target time.

Usage

ef_regionalize(
  data,
  variable,
  covariates,
  method,
  use_qc,
  surface_covariates,
  grid = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  station_covariates = NULL,
  prediction = ef_predict_control()
)

Arguments

data

The regionalization input: a data frame with the columns station_id, lon, lat (decimal degrees, WGS84), target_time (POSIXct UTC), variable, value (unit of the contract), qc_status ("ok", "warning", "excluded") and, optionally, elevation [m], period_seconds and reference (required for etr_inst and etr_24), as in dev/specs/weather-forcing.md section 7.2; or the result of ef_station_qc() for a variable observed at the stations.

variable

Character, one of "air_temperature" (degC), "vapour_pressure" (kPa), "wind_speed_2m" (m s-1), "clearness" (-), "solar_radiation" (W m-2), "etr_inst" (mm h-1), "etr_24" (mm d-1).

covariates

NULL or a SpatRaster on the working grid, one named layer per covariate (e.g. elevation [m], distance_to_coast [km]). GWR and the global regression use all its layers; the lapse-rate variant of C1 uses elevation. Cells where any layer is NA are outside the domain for every method (value NA, flag EF_INPUT_NA), so that the surfaces of C1, C2 and C3 cover the same cells.

method

A method object from ef_method_gwr(), ef_method_station(), ef_method_ols() or ef_method_idw(); no default.

use_qc

Character, no default: the QC statuses that enter the fits, among "ok" and "warning" ("excluded" never does). Recorded in the provenance.

surface_covariates

Character, no default when the method uses covariates: the covariates derived from the surface state (e.g. "lst", "ndvi"), or character(0) if none. Decision GW-07 is open: using them is allowed only when declared here, and they raise EF_GWR_SURFACE_COVARIATE (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 2.7).

grid

NULL or a SpatRaster template of the working grid (geometry only); required when covariates is NULL, and with the same geometry otherwise.

exclude

NULL or a data frame with columns station_id and reason: stations excluded by the user.

station_covariates

NULL or a data frame with station_id and the covariates used, to take the covariates at the stations from a table (e.g. elevation of the metadata) instead of extracting them from the rasters (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md section 2.2, GW-10).

prediction

Prediction settings from ef_predict_control().

Value

An object of class c("earthflux_surface", "list") with:

  • surface: SpatRaster, one layer per target time, named <variable>_<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>, in the unit of the variable (in memory or in prediction$filename);

  • flag_word: integer SpatRaster, one layer per target time (flags_<layer>), with the bits of flag_bits: 0 = conditions evaluated and none active (dev/specs/flags.md section 6.3);

  • flag_bits: data frame bit, code, severity, description;

  • uncertainty: NULL (prediction variance not delivered, GW-19);

  • variable, unit, target_time (POSIXct), method (exact name: "gwr", "global_ols", "idw", "station", "station_lapse"), method_settings (the method object);

  • diagnostics: named list, one fitted object per target time (earthflux_gwr, earthflux_ols, earthflux_idw or earthflux_station_forcing);

  • station_table: one row per target time and station: coordinates (WGS84 and projected [m]), metadata elevation, QC status, observed value, covariates used, status ("used"/"excluded"), exclusion_reason, fitted, residual, loo_fitted and loo_residual (C1: error at the other stations; the representative station has NA);

  • flags: object and record flags (see Details);

  • provenance: method and settings, variable, unit, reference, target times, covariates and their source, surface covariates, QC policy and exclusions, CRS and distance method, prediction settings (mode, block rows, number of blocks, chunk rows, file names without directories), execution plan (future backend and workers, versions, seed, terra options, elapsed time), package versions and flags (registry rows, bit table, counts per layer and code, policies, flags of each fit) and flags_evaluated.

Details

Flags. Cell scope, in the flag word (bits of the GWR stage, dev/specs/flags.md section 6.4): EF_INPUT_NA (bit 0, a covariate is NA), EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_COVARIATE (1; GWR and OLS), EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_LOCAL (2; GWR with compact kernels), EF_GWR_OUTSIDE_HULL (3; GWR, OLS, IDW), EF_GWR_FEW_NEIGHBOURS (4) and EF_GWR_LOCAL_SINGULAR (5; GWR), and EF_GWR_OUT_OF_DOMAIN (6, class III, critical): the prediction is outside the physical domain of the variable (air temperature <= -273.15 degC, vapour pressure <= 0, wind speed, clearness, solar radiation or daily reference ET < 0, instantaneous reference ET <= 0). Out-of-domain values are kept and flagged, never truncated; their consumers reject them with earthflux_domain_error. Counts per layer and code are in provenance$flags$counts. Object scope: EF_GWR_SINGLE_STATION (C1), EF_GWR_SURFACE_COVARIATE (declared surface covariates) and the object flags of the fits (e.g. EF_GWR_BW_AT_BOUND); record scope: EF_GWR_STATION_EXCLUDED (rows of station_table).

Errors. earthflux_missing_input (method, use_qc, surface_covariates, grid, columns of data), earthflux_input_error (duplicated records per station and target time, inconsistent station locations, geographic or non-metric CRS, undeclared surface covariates, unknown representative station, files that exist without overwrite), earthflux_domain_error (infinite values, longitude or latitude out of range) and the errors of the methods (e.g. earthflux_gwr_insufficient_stations). Files written by a call that fails are removed.

Parallel processing

Sequential by default. If the user has set a future plan with more than one worker (e.g. future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2)), the fits (one per target time) and the prediction blocks are evaluated with future.apply::future_lapply() (future.seed = TRUE); EarthFlux never sets a plan nor changes terra or R options. The results are identical for any plan, number of workers and block size; the plan used is recorded in provenance$execution. A SpatRaster keeps a pointer to terra memory: save the result with filename or terra::wrap(), not with saveRDS() alone.

Verification status

Methods: see ef_method_gwr() (C3, CANDIDATA (corroborada)), ef_method_ols(), ef_method_idw() (CANDIDATA) and ef_method_station(). Projection, extraction and block prediction are design choices (dev/specs/gwr-forcing.md sections 2.1, 2.2, 6.1).

See also

ef_regionalize_cv() for cross-validation with the same inputs; ef_gwr_fit() and ef_gwr_predict() for the numeric core.

Other spatial regionalization functions: ef_gwr_bandwidth(), ef_gwr_diagnostics(), ef_gwr_fit(), ef_gwr_predict(), ef_gwr_search(), ef_method_gwr(), ef_method_idw(), ef_method_ols(), ef_method_station(), ef_predict_control(), ef_regionalize_cv(), ef_spatial_folds()

Examples

# \donttest{
# Synthetic 20 x 20 km grid (UTM 19S) with elevation, and 12 stations
grid <- terra::rast(nrows = 20, ncols = 20, xmin = 300000, xmax = 320000,
                    ymin = 6100000, ymax = 6120000, crs = "EPSG:32719")
xy <- terra::crds(grid)
terra::values(grid) <- 200 + 0.02 * (xy[, 1] - 300000)
names(grid) <- "elevation"
sx <- 300500 + 1000 * c(1, 4, 8, 12, 17, 2, 6, 10, 15, 18, 5, 13)
sy <- 6100500 + 1000 * c(2, 15, 6, 11, 3, 9, 18, 1, 16, 8, 12, 5)
ll <- terra::project(cbind(sx, sy), from = "EPSG:32719", to = "EPSG:4326")
z <- 200 + 0.02 * (sx - 300000)
data <- data.frame(
  station_id = sprintf("S%02d", 1:12), lon = ll[, 1], lat = ll[, 2],
  elevation = z, target_time = as.POSIXct("2024-01-15 14:30", tz = "UTC"),
  period_seconds = 0L, variable = "air_temperature",
  value = 25 - 0.0065 * z + c(0.2, -0.1, 0.3, 0, -0.2, 0.1, 0, -0.3,
                              0.2, 0.1, -0.1, 0),
  qc_status = "ok", reference = NA_character_
)
ta <- ef_regionalize(data, "air_temperature", covariates = grid,
                     method = ef_method_ols(), use_qc = "ok",
                     surface_covariates = character(0))
ta
#> <earthflux_surface>
#> Variable: air_temperature [degC]; method: global_ols; 1 target time(s)
#> Grid: 20 x 20 cells (in memory)
#> Stations: 12 used, 0 excluded (records over all target times)
#> Cell flags (cells over all layers):
#>   EF_GWR_EXTRAPOLATION_COVARIATE: 40
#>   EF_GWR_OUTSIDE_HULL: 176
ta$surface
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 20, 20, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 300000, 320000, 6100000, 6120000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 19S (EPSG:32719)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : air_temperature_20240115T143000Z
#> min value   :                         21.14085
#> max value   :                        23.690391
# }
